review_notes: I read the whole file and the relevant definitions in Definitions/Def_CerednikDrinfeld_FormalUpperHalfPlaneChartRings.lean (edgeRel, edgeQuot.mk, mk_edgeRel). The only simp-interface issue I found is that the new definition ψ has no characterizing rewrite lemmas for its two generator cases (constants and variables). Every proof unfolds ψ with `rw [ψ, ...]` and repeats the same RHS. I did not run Lean. I did not check how the Mathlib simp set would treat the proposed lemmas, so the suggested ψ_C and ψ_X simp attributes are untested. The rest of the file (the theorem statements, the `(0 + 1)` exponent, the πQ and Q₁ abbrevs) is fixed by the target statement or has no clear simp problem.

findings.problem: ψ is a plain def built from eval₂Hom, but it has no basic evaluation lemmas for its constructors. There is no `ψ_C` for constants. `ψ_X` exists but is not tagged @[simp], and it is stated after ψ_comp_map, which does not use it. ψ_comp_map therefore unfolds ψ by hand with `rw [..., ψ, MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom_C, Ideal.quotientMap_mk, ...]` and `rw [..., ψ, MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom_X']`. It also uses `show` to restate the goal. ψ_X repeats the same `rw [ψ, eval₂Hom_X']` unfolding. Any simp-based use of ψ must unfold the definition, which exposes the `eval₂Hom`/`quotientMap` implementation and not a stable normal form.
findings.proposed_change: State a `ψ_C (a : 𝒪 ⧸ Ideal.span {π}) : ψ 𝒪 π (MvPolynomial.C a) = Ideal.quotientMap … a` in terms of an exposed form. Alternatively, state the constant case of ψ_comp_map as the lemma. Prove it once by `rw [ψ, MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom_C]`. Move ψ_X (tagged @[simp]) above ψ_comp_map so both generator cases are simp-normal. Then prove ψ_comp_map by `ringHom_ext` followed by `simp [ψ_C, ψ_X]`, or by `rw [MvPolynomial.map_X, ψ_X]`, and drop the `show` restatements. Keep ψ itself irreducible to simp, so no caller unfolds it.
findings.benefit: The mathematical content of ψ (it sends the constant a to the image of a, and X i to the class of X i) is available as simp lemmas. Proofs such as ψ_comp_map and ψ_X_mul_X can use `simp` or a short `rw` and no longer depend on how ψ is built from eval₂Hom. The repeated `ψ, eval₂Hom_X'` unfolding disappears.
